hypothesis: An evidence-first DeepSeek reranker rubric will reduce technically conflicting or unprovable final selections by prioritizing explicit tender requirements and catalog evidence over retrieval rank.
why_now: Current scored failures are selection failures; no unresolved taxonomy case is proven to be a retrieval miss. The existing reranker prompt remains a general checklist.
expected_effect: Better selection among retrieved close variants, especially explicit ball-valve passage/execution conflicts and incomplete candidate evidence, while preserving recall and output behavior.
expected_metric_gain: +3.3–6.7 pp public hard-pass and approximately +3.3 pp blind hard-pass; safety metrics should not regress.
lesson_from_history: Broad candidate gating (Cycle 1) and compatibility evidence injection (Cycle 2) regressed, so this change adds neither filtering nor extraction. Cycles 3–4 validated additive canonicalization but plateaued on aggregate metrics.
candidate_hypotheses: Evidence-first reranker decision rubric for passage/execution and evidence completeness (selected).
Explicit flange-subtype schema and candidate interpretation.
Index-time catalog-text enrichment for aliases and normalized properties.
plan_summary: Created and strict-validated proposal, capability spec, design, and implementation-only tasks in openspec/changes/cycle-05-evidence-first-reranker-rubric/. No product code or evaluation artifacts were changed.
